evidence: typography_tex.py:1026 now sets the bottom bound to \OSScanLink@top-\textheight-\maxdepth. TeX allows the last box on a page to hang that far below the text block, so a link on the bottom baseline can keep its glyph depth below the bound.
scan_links.py is unchanged: the box runs from y+dy-depth to y+dy+height, and the check is box[2] >= bottom (line 31). The bottom bound is the only thing that changed, as intended.

test_scan_link_placement.py:73-79 sets baseline=100, depth=2 and bottom=95. The box bottom is 98, which is at least 95, so the expected result dx=0, dy=0 is correct. Without the maxdepth term, bottom would be 100 and 98 < 100 would push the link off the line, so the test would catch a regression.

The sampled link rectangles in /tmp/scan-link-output-qa.json are the same as the ones approved last time. Hebrew: n5 [89.877,680.899,100.248,690.284] and n7 [77.514,...,87.885,...]. Parallel: n5, n6, n7 and n8 are unchanged. Each is 10.371 x 9.385pt. The fix did not move any sampled link, as expected, because none of them sits on a last baseline.
findings.residual_nonblocking: A symbol deeper than \maxdepth (5pt at 10pt in book.cls) could still move up a row on the last line. The current arrow's whole rectangle is 9.385pt including link padding, so its depth is well under that. This needs no action unless the symbol or font changes.

findings.note: This still applies: no test exercises the ±2 row limit on its own. This minor gap does not block approval.
Identical arrows are placed nearest the text first, so their order beside a line can run against the reading direction.
In HTML, several boundaries on a column's final line can add height to the gutter row. No text width is used, and identical vertical height is not promised.
The 'margin full' build failure is intentional. No full-book PDF regression was run.
